11.0.0.en: God calls His people in the kingdom of Judah, through Jeremiah, to renew the covenant with God; and whoever refuses this covenant is cursed, that is, deprived of God's blessings.

11.1.0.en: Iron furnace: a furnace that reaches a very high temperature, above 1500 degrees Fahrenheit, to melt iron.

11.1.1.en: God reminds His people of the covenant He made with them through Moses, when He brought them out of the land of Egypt and saved them from the harsh humiliation of slavery, whose hardship He likens to an iron furnace, and He commanded them to obey His commandments, so that He would be their God and shepherd them, and they would become His people.

11.2.0.en: God's promise in His covenant with His people was to give them a land full of good things, which is expressed by saying that it flows with milk and honey, namely the fertile land of Canaan, which God gave to His people after they crossed the wilderness of Sinai. Remarkably, He says “as it is this day” while they were already dwelling in Canaan; so the land full of good things can only mean the heavenly Jerusalem, full of the spiritual blessings that He gives to His children who keep His commandments.

11.2.1.en: Jeremiah answered on behalf of the people who fear God, who are sadly very few, and said Amen, that is, he declared his agreement with this covenant, to keep God's commandments and so receive His eternal blessings.

11.3.0.en: God asked Jeremiah to proclaim in Jerusalem and Judea that God calls His people to renew the covenant with Him.

11.4.0.en: God reminds His people that He had repeatedly called them to obey His commandments early, from the time they were in Egypt until the days of Jeremiah.

11.5.0.en: God shows that the cause of the afflictions His people are going through is their refusal to obey His commandments, their abandoning His covenant, and their being swept along by their evil desires.

11.5.1.en: God, in His fatherhood, seeks you so that you may return to Him, and reminds you of your sonship to Him, which opens for you the doors of divine blessings. So remember at the beginning of every day that you were born of God in the sacrament of Baptism, so that you may enjoy fellowship with Him and incline to doing good at all times.

11.6.s.en: (2) The results of breaking the covenant

11.6.0.en: Conspiracy: a plot, a coup and a rebellion against the leader of the people, who is God. God showed Jeremiah that there was a rebellion among the people and that they refused to submit to God, their leader.

11.7.0.en: God shows the details of this conspiracy as follows:

11.7.1.en: 1- The people's return to the sins of their fathers, which are the various evil desires.

11.7.3.en: 3- The breaking of their covenant of allegiance, sonship and obedience to God's commandments.

11.8.0.en: As a result of the people's breaking their covenant with God, they deprive themselves of His care and protection, and so they are exposed to a great affliction, namely the Babylonian invasion and the captivity; and when they call on God, He will not answer them because of their immersion in evil and the worship of idols.

11.9.0.en: The inhabitants of Jerusalem and Judea will take refuge in the pagan gods to save them from the attack of Babylon, but these will do nothing for them, because they are merely statues.

11.10.0.en: God declares with sorrow how deeply they were immersed in the worship of idols, for they made a god for every city, indeed for every street of Jerusalem, and they made altars for the pagan gods in these streets; and the weakness and shame of these gods appeared when they asked for their help and the gods could do nothing.

11.11.0.en: God speaks to His prophet Jeremiah, showing how firmly His people cling to evil, and tells him not to pray for them, for prayer will not profit them because they have not repented.

11.11.1.en: If you meet with hard afflictions, examine yourself, lest you yourself be the cause of your distance from God or of your immersion in some troublesome sin, so that you may repent and be delivered from your troubles.

11.12.0.en: Although God's people have rejected His covenant, and no prayer on their behalf can any longer profit them, He loves them as His bride and calls her “my beloved.” God is astonished at their doing evil in His house and at their disobedience to His commandments and laws; their worship became superficial, so they were deprived of God's blessings, which are expressed by the holy flesh that God sanctifies for His house when they offer their sacrifices and eat of their flesh. But now the holy flesh has become ordinary flesh, which they eat with lust, and this made them lose the blessing; their delight has become the doing of evil and not the worship of God.

11.13.0.en: God cared for His people and shepherded them and gave them peace and tranquility when they kept His commandments and had spiritual fruits, which are the various virtues. Therefore He likened them to a green olive tree, that is, one full of life, with fruit upon it, that is, olives containing oil, which signifies the work of the Holy Spirit. But when they rejected His covenant, He allowed the armies of Babylon to attack them and burn their city Jerusalem; so they attacked it with noise and shouting and broke its branches after they had demolished it.

11.14.0.en: God allowed affliction and evil to come upon Jerusalem and Judea because they had done many evils. For although God is the planter of this olive tree, He left it to be broken and burned, since their evils came upon them because of their provoking Him, and the result was their ruin through God's abandoning them. Their worship of foreign gods, chiefly the worship of Baal, is the cause of their disaster.

11.14.1.en: Remember that your natural place is the bosom of God, and you will live in tranquility, your life will be filled with virtues, and you will protect yourself from the wars of the demons, because you are under God's protection.

11.15.0.en: God made Jeremiah know what would happen to the kingdom of Judah, and He also made him know their plots against him and their attempt to kill him because of his rebuking them.

11.16.0.en: Domesticated: tame, raised in private houses and pens.

11.16.1.en: Jeremiah complains to God that he lived in familiarity with his people and in fatherly love, like the lamb that they raise in their houses, yet they treacherously rose against him to slaughter and kill him. He also likens himself to a tree that they try to uproot together with its fruit, that is, they kill him and he becomes one of the dead. All this is because he loves them and rebukes them so that they may return to God by repentance. This is a clear prophecy about Christ, for Jeremiah is a type of Him, because Christ preached to them His Kingdom and called them to repentance, and they rose against Him and crucified Him, but by His death He saved us from our sins.

11.17.0.en: I have revealed my cause: I have presented my complaint.

11.17.1.en: He calls upon God, who knows the hearts of men and the evil or good they hide in them, to take vengeance for their evils and discipline them with His punishment, that perhaps they may repent. For he does not ask for vengeance upon them out of anger against them, but for their discipline, that they may repent, because they are his children. He has presented his complaint to God, who is able to do all things; therefore he calls Him the Lord of hosts.

11.18.0.en: Anathoth: a nearby city lying north of Jerusalem, in which Jeremiah was born and raised.

11.18.1.en: Everyone rose against Jeremiah because he rebuked them, even the people of his own town Anathoth, who tried to prevent him from prophesying and proclaiming the voice of God, and threatened to kill him if he did this.

11.19.0.en: God declares that He will punish the kingdom of Judah: the strong young men will die by the sword of the army of Babylon, while the daughters, who represent the weak among the people, will die of hunger as a result of the siege of Jerusalem. All this is because of their refusal to hear the voice of God from the mouth of Jeremiah.

11.20.0.en: God declares that He will punish the city of Anathoth with a severe punishment, annihilating and destroying it, because it should have been the first to hear the words of their prophet Jeremiah, since he was from it.

11.20.1.en: If you fall into affliction, present your complaint to God before any human being, for He loves you more than all, and at the same time is able to rescue you from all people.

11.20.2.en: The temporary success of the wicked and then their destruction

12.0.s.en: (1) The temporary success of the wicked

12.0.0.en: Plead with You: become an adversary to You.

12.0.1.en: Jeremiah dares to discuss with God the success of the wicked, because he is weary of their cruelty and their abuse toward him. But he begins to speak with humility, saying that God is righteous and holy and too high for him to stand before as an adversary and argue with, for he is a lowly man; yet he asks in order to learn what is God's wisdom in the governance of mankind. For his mind does not understand why the wicked prosper in their material lives and wield authority and abuse the children of God; indeed, through their confidence in their authority and their evil they have become secure and sure of their ability to abuse the righteous. Here he repeats the words of the Psalm (Ps 119:137).

12.1.0.en: Jeremiah traced the wicked back to God's good works toward them, for it is He who gave them blessings represented by material goods and fruits, but sadly they used them for evil and forsook God. In addition they fell into the sin of hypocrisy, for they spoke of God and offered worship with the mouth, but they rejected God from within, which the verse expresses by “their kidneys,” the plural of kidney.

12.1.1.en: Some think that when King Josiah, who took care to build the temple, remove the idols and spread the word of God, was killed in his battle with Pharaoh Necho, king of Egypt, the wicked who worship idols rejoiced over him and abused all the righteous, Jeremiah first among them; so from the depth of affliction Jeremiah uttered these words, crying to God to rescue him from their hands.

12.2.0.en: Jeremiah reminds God that he is one of His own, for God knows Jeremiah's heart, his faith and his life with Him, so that He may rescue him from the wicked and then discipline them so that they may repent. He likens them to sheep that God prepares for slaughter and announces to them that He will destroy them, that perhaps they may fear and repent; so he asks God's help to lift the abuses of the wicked from him and to frighten them with destruction at the hand of Babylon, so that they may return to God. For being set apart for slaughter, or being appointed for killing, does not mean that they are slaughtered or killed, but that they are prepared for killing, so that when they see death coming upon them they may repent and leave their evils.

12.3.0.en: Jeremiah likens the land to a sorrowful woman weeping over what has happened to her, for her people, that is, the crops sown in her, have withered, food has become scarce and hunger has increased, besides the death of the beasts and the birds. All this is from God's anger against the wicked Jews who dwell in the kingdom of Judah, who worshiped idols and abandoned the worship of God and persisted in their unclean desires, and in pride made light of the divine wrath coming upon them, which was meant to lead them to repent, and said, “God does not see our last end,” that is, He does not know our fate, instead of letting the affliction lead them to repentance so that they might have a good end with God.

12.3.1.en: Some of the Fathers see that the land that mourns means the angel responsible for the land of Judah, who weeps over their evils and their making light of the divine wrath, because every kingdom has an angel who intercedes for it before God.

12.3.2.en: Do not be disturbed by the success of the wicked, their authority, their threats, and their contempt for your faithfulness and purity, but persevere in your striving, confident that God is with you and supports you and will gladden your heart in the end, when all the greatness of the wicked passes away and they are cast into eternal torment.

12.4.0.en: God reproaches Jeremiah for his weakness and his not enduring the abuses of the wicked, and makes clear that He allowed him afflictions in proportion to his spiritual stature, but that there are greater afflictions that He did not allow him. He likens his affliction to a race in running with a group of men; this is what happened with Jeremiah in his not enduring the wicked. But if he entered a race running with horses, like his entering into direct war with the demons, this would be far harder than enduring the abuses of the wicked around him.

12.4.1.en: He gives another comparison for the abuses that happen to Jeremiah: he is in a land of peace, that is, an easy valley, yet he was not able to walk in it but fell and sprawled on his face; so how will he walk in the Jordan during its flooding? He will not be able to cross it because of its depth and will surely drown. So God assures him that He allowed him trials within his capacity, and that He is with him, supporting him in them, so he should not be disturbed.

12.5.0.en: They have called a multitude after you: they have said evil words against you and rebuked you to prevent you from prophesying.

12.5.1.en: God makes clear to Jeremiah that He feels with him and with all that he suffers, for He knows that the people of his city Anathoth, that is, his brothers and relatives, have forsaken him and stood against him and tried to prevent him from proclaiming the word of God. He warns him not to entrust himself to them even if they speak kind words to him, for they are wicked and treacherous, and he must be on guard against them.

12.5.2.en: Be reassured that God does not allow you a trial beyond your strength; He feels all your suffering, sympathizes with you, supports you and protects you from the plots of the wicked. He is your God who loves you and protects you and brings you out of all afflictions and gives you consolations, and then the glories of the Kingdom.

12.6.s.en: (3) The evils of the Jews and their shepherds

12.6.0.en: Because of the evils of the kingdom of Judah, God was compelled to abandon them and to allow them to be killed and taken captive by Babylon. But His fatherhood made Him grieve over them and call them “my house, my heritage and my beloved.” He wished that they would remain in His worship and enjoy His care, and so receive their eternal inheritance that He had prepared for them.

12.6.1.en: If only you would remember God's love toward you and His longing to take you into His embrace, and that you are the temple of God and set apart for Him, so that you may refuse sin however dear it is to your heart and however accustomed you are to it or however much people encourage you in it. Do not wound God's feelings, but refuse sin for His sake, lest you deprive yourself of His love and be exposed to eternal destruction.

12.7.0.en: With sorrow God likens His people to a lion standing against Him, using the abilities He gave it to defy Him by its evils and its worship of idols. And He made the holy Promised Land a wasteland, and all holiness departed from it, so He called it rugged. And instead of uttering praise to God, it murmured against Him and spoke evil words against Him and provoked Him by its sins. Because of all this evil God hated it, that is, hated its sins, and was compelled to abandon it and to discipline it, that perhaps it might repent and return to Him.

12.8.0.en: He continues to show His people's defiance of Him and makes clear their violence, cruelty and persistence in evil, likening them to one of the birds of prey that swoop down on their prey and tear its flesh; so God's people abused Him and defiled His temple and His holy city Jerusalem with idols.

12.8.1.en: He likens them also to the hyena, for its cruelty and its preying on other animals, just as every man wrongs his companion.

12.8.2.en: Therefore God allowed the army of Babylon to besiege Jerusalem and swoop down on it and destroy it, like the birds of prey that swoop down on their prey.

12.8.3.en: And He likens the Jews, the inhabitants of Jerusalem and Judea, to the beasts of the field, which the many wild beasts easily devour, that is, the armies of Babylon, which kill and destroy the kingdom of Judah.

12.9.0.en: God grieves because the shepherds of His people, that is, the kings, rulers, priests and false prophets, have led His people astray; so God abandoned them and they were exposed to ruin and destruction at the hand of Babylon, even though they are His people, set apart for life with Him, whom God desires and whom He wished to live with Him.

12.10.0.en: They have made it desolate: He continues His speech from the previous verse, that the shepherds made Jerusalem and Judea desolate by turning the people away from God and not teaching the truth, so that it was attacked and its land laid waste. Being desolate it mourns unto Me: the people mourn on God's shoulder, and in another translation “they sob before Me,” after it became desolate; but the weeping of the shepherds and the people over the desolation of the kingdom of Judah was sadly not repentance, and they did not return to God with right faith, but was merely being moved by the calamity that had happened. The whole land is made desolate, because no man lays it to heart: no one put God in his heart and no one repented, so the desolation and the captivity continued for seventy years.

12.10.1.en: The shepherds did not do their duty and turned the people away from God, so the kingdom of Judah was laid waste; and when it was laid waste, they wept over it, but not with the weeping of repentance and return to God.

12.11.0.en: High places: the plural of “height,” that is, a hill or an elevated place.

12.11.1.en: The army of Babylon attacked the kingdom of Judah and laid waste the valleys and the high places, which are where the Jews had built temples for idols; they demolished and plundered everything precious in them and killed with the sword whomever they met. Thus all the Jews were in fear and terror, because everyone was exposed to killing, plunder and destruction. And he calls “the sword of Babylon” “the sword of the LORD,” since God is the One who allowed Babylon to discipline His people, that they might repent and return to their first faith.

12.12.0.en: God withheld the blessing from His children dwelling in Jerusalem and Judea, so that when they sowed their fields they did not yield the required fruits but very poor crops, expressed by thorns, that is, the lack of blessing, just as the earth gave Adam of old thorns and thistles instead of the leafy plants full of fruit that were in Paradise. So their labor in farming or industry or any craft was of no avail, and they were put to shame at not obtaining fruits and produce from their labor. This was because of God's fierce anger against them, which He showed them with the aim of calling them to repentance.

12.12.1.en: If some of your work is hindered, or you enter into material afflictions or problems that have no solution by any human means, ask yourself: is God pleased with you? And if you are in a relationship with Him, are you growing spiritually, or have you left your first love and the service you used to serve? God loves you and seeks you by every way so that you may return to His embrace.

12.13.s.en: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

12.13.1.en: The inheritance which I have caused My people Israel to inherit: the land of Canaan, that is, the Promised Land.

12.13.2.en: This is a prophecy about the nations that live around the people of God, whether near or far, whom God allowed to assault and lay waste the land of His people, such as Assyria and Babylon. So God prophesies against them by the mouth of Jeremiah that He will lay them waste as He laid waste the kingdom of Israel and will lay waste the kingdom of Judah.

12.14.0.en: Then God prophesies concerning His people that after they are plucked from their land, taken captive and their cities laid waste, He will have mercy on them and bring them back again from captivity, so that they build their cities and offer the worship of God in His temple in Jerusalem.

12.15.0.en: As for the nations that taught God's people the worship of idols, the most famous of which is the worship of Baal and swearing by him, if these believe in God and repent and leave their sins, God will have mercy on them and will again build them up after having laid them waste. This is what happened when the Gentiles believed in Christianity, and they became living stones in the Church, built up in the spiritual building, walking in the way of God and calling upon His name.

12.16.0.en: But the pagan nations that persist in their evils, God will lay waste and destroy, and they will not be built again. This is a type of the eternal destruction of the wicked who persist in their sins.

12.16.1.en: God is merciful and does not desire the destruction of mankind, even of those who defy Him; so be confident that He loves you whatever evils you have done, and return to Him, and He will wash you from your sins and build you up, and you will become great and pure and fit for the Kingdom of Heaven that He has prepared for you.

12.16.2.en: The fruits of pride and evil desires (1) The linen girdle (vv. 1-11:)

12.16.3.en: 1- Thus saith the LORD unto me, Go and get thee a linen girdle, and put it upon thy loins, and put it not in water. 2- So I got a girdle according to the word of the LORD, and put it on my loins. 3- And the word of the LORD came unto me the second time, saying, 4- Take the girdle that thou hast got, which is upon thy loins, and arise, go to Euphrates, and hide it there in a hole of the rock. 5- So I went, and hid it by Euphrates, as the LORD commanded me. 6- And it came to pass after many days, that the LORD said unto me, Arise, go to Euphrates, and take the girdle from thence, which I commanded thee to hide there.

12.16.4.en: 7- Then I went to Euphrates, and digged, and took the girdle from the place where I had hid it: and, behold, the girdle was marred, it was profitable for nothing. 8- Then the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 9- Thus saith the LORD, After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem. 10- This evil people, which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the imagination of their heart, and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.

12.16.5.en: 11- For as the girdle cleaveth to the loins of a man, so have I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah, saith the LORD; that they might be unto me for a people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory: but they would not hear.
